inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 273M shares issued at 2026-06-30 (10-Q balance sheet) + 2M dilutive share-based awards (Q2-26 EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award withholding) is expensed in the flows. July-Sept 2026 buybacks are excluded from both the count and the cash, so the anchor is internally consistent.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Pro forma for the Pizza Hut divestitures: total debt 12,285 at 2026-06-30 (short-term borrowings 2,813 incl. revolver + long-term debt 9,462 + finance leases) less cash 674, less 25 cash classified in assets held for sale, less ~2,300 net after-tax proceeds (10-Q Note 3: 'approximately $2.3 billion of net proceeds after taxes, closing adjustments and transaction-contingent fees'). China Pizza Hut sale to Yum China ($1.2bn) closed 2026-08-07 (8-K); Pizza Hut ex-China sale to LongRange/Toppings TopCo ($1.488bn) closed 2026-09-01 (8-K). Management will repay the revolver and set the remainder aside for buybacks under a new $4bn authorization. The $75M earn-out is contingent and excluded.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back) TTM Jun-26 = 70 + 35 - 37 = 68; plus 'Employee share-based award exercises' cash (equity statement, net-share-settlement withholding) TTM = 49 + 29 - 42 = 36. YUM publishes no combined figure, so the two are summed: 104.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM Jun-26 repurchases 552 + 674 - 338 = 888 (cash flow statement). YUM is a persistent repurchaser, so the flat count is funded. A further ~$2bn of Pizza Hut proceeds is earmarked for buybacks under a $4bn authorization through June 2028; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.fy0: TTM Jun-2026 pro forma ex-Pizza Hut
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.85 (defensive QSR franchisor, but ~3.4x pro forma net debt/EBITDA) -> cost of equity ~8.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (10-Q: 96% fixed at ~4.5% effective), after-tax ~3.5%. Market weights ~80/20 equity/debt (37.4bn market cap vs 9.3bn pro forma net debt) -> ~7.6%; 7.5% used. Same WACC in all scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (restaurant rent) sits inside restaurant expenses and therefore inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. Finance leases are small and inside total debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.fy0_build: TTM Jun-26 consolidated revenue 8,722 (FY25 8,214 + H1-26 4,228 - H1-25 3,720) less Pizza Hut Division TTM revenue ~1,046 (FY25 1,013 per 10-K Note segment table; H1-26 507; H1-25 ~474) = 7,676. TTM Operating Profit 2,703 + Special Items 105 (FY25 122 + H1-26 38 - H1-25 55) + D&A 236 = 3,044 adjusted EBITDA; less Pizza Hut Division EBITDA ~343 (OP 340+135-155 = 320, D&A ~23); less ~40 of recurring-looking refranchising gains (FY25 unallocated +48); plus SBC 68 (engine wants pre-SBC EBITDA) -> ~2,730 pre-SBC, 35.5% of ex-PH revenue. Corporate G&A stranded costs after the sale are assumed partly offset by TSA/Byte fees from Pizza Hut. D&A ex-PH ~213 (2.8%); capex ex-PH ~377 (4.9%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (engine route). Routing: YUM is an operating company (asset-light QSR franchisor: ~98% franchised KFC/Taco Bell, plus company-operated Taco Bell US, KFC UK/Germany and Habit). It is not a bank, REIT, insurer, LIC or holdco, so the SKILL.md routing table sends it to owner-FCF. The negative book equity (shareholders' deficit -7,107 at 2026-06-30) is the product of the 2016 leveraged recap/Yum China spin and decades of buybacks; it disqualifies book-value models (BVPS compounding, residual income) but does not affect an unlevered DCF, which values the franchise cash flows and deducts the debt once in the bridge. Unlevered build: interest expense (~$500M/yr) is NOT in the flows; net debt is deducted once. PORTFOLIO CHANGE: Pizza Hut was sold in two transactions closing 2026-08-07 and 2026-09-01, so FY0 is a pro forma TTM ex-Pizza Hut base and the proceeds are in net debt; the historical CSV (and reported_fcf/last_fcf) still includes Pizza Hut. last_fcf here is the levered reported TTM FCF (1,679 = OCF 2,083 - capex 404) less SBC incl. withholding (104); it is a reference figure only -- the engine builds unlevered flows from components. Q2-26 GAAP net income (853) includes a 449 special tax benefit (359 deferred-tax recognition on Pizza Hut basis, 91 IP step-up) that is non-recurring and excluded. Near-term: Taco Bell US lettuce recall (Taylor Farms, July 2026) guided TB US company margin to 19-21% for Q3-26 -- reflected in a softer Y1 margin. IRS 2014 reorganization dispute (Tax Court, $2.1bn tax + $0.42bn penalties + ~$2.1bn interest) is carried as a probability-weighted equity-bridge deduction.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close; not an after-hours print. Near the bottom of the 52-week range.

equity_bridge.note: 10-K FY2025 Note 20 / MD&A Contingencies: IRS asserts ~$2.1bn tax + $418M penalties + ~$2.1bn accrued interest (to 2025-12-31) on ~$6.0bn alleged taxable distributions; YUM petitioned the Tax Court 2025-06-04. Carried at ~20% probability of an adverse outcome on a ~$4.6bn gross claim. Not in total_debt.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr/5yr_cagr blended, adjusted for the Pizza Hut exit (Pizza Hut grew slowest, so ex-PH system growth runs higher) and for the 2025-26 company-store acquisitions that inflated reported revenue
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR undefined: shareholders' equity has been negative since 2016 (leveraged recap and buybacks). EPS 5yr CAGR (13.3%) starts from the COVID-depressed FY2020 base and is not a forward guide.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history = reported FCF - SBC (cash-flow add-back); equity-award withholding not reconstructed before FY2024, so the historical owner series uses the add-back only. FY2025 1,569, FY2022 1,064, FY2020 1,048. Owner-FCF CAGRs run ABOVE reported because SBC has fallen (97 in FY2020 -> 70 in FY2025) -- SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. All historical series include Pizza Hut. Revenue 3yr/5yr from FY2022/FY2020 to FY2025 (FY2020 the first full post-2016-refranchising comparable base).

base.narrative: KFC international (90% of units, ~5% net new units/yr) and Taco Bell US + international compound system sales ~6-7%; franchise-royalty mix lifts margin ~3.5pp over the decade as the lower-margin Pizza Hut drag is gone and Taco Bell recovers from the July-2026 lettuce recall within a year.
base.capex_rationale: Elevated near term by Taco Bell US/KFC UK-Germany company-store development and Byte by Yum! tech, easing as the company-store build slows.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: ETR ex-special items 20.3-22.7% (2025-26); OBBBA provisions favorable. Cash rate on unlevered EBIT ~21-22%.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-Pizza Hut YUM is a two-engine franchisor: KFC (international unit growth in emerging markets, Yum China master licence) and Taco Bell (US value leadership plus early international scaling). System sales grow ~6-7% from ~5% unit growth plus low single-digit same-store sales; Taco Bell's lettuce-recall hit fades through H1 FY2027; refranchising-style royalty mix and G&A leverage lift the EBITDA margin from ~34.5% to ~38%. Proceeds go to revolver repayment and buybacks, keeping leverage near ~3.5x. The IRS 2014 case is carried at expected value.
scenario_narratives.bull: KFC net unit growth holds at the upper end (~6%+) in India, Africa, Middle East and Southeast Asia, Taco Bell's international pipeline finally scales and its US value positioning keeps taking share in a cautious-consumer QSR market; Byte by Yum! digital/AI ordering drives same-store sales and franchisee margins. With Pizza Hut gone, the portfolio's growth rate and margin re-rate toward pure-play franchisor peers; EBITDA margin reaches 40%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Western-brand boycotts in the Middle East/Southeast Asia and a slower Yum China cadence cap KFC unit growth; Taco Bell's food-safety recall leaves a lasting traffic scar and US QSR value wars compress same-store sales and franchisee health; GLP-1 adoption and delivery-aggregator costs weigh on traffic. Growth slows to ~3-4%, margins stall near 34%, stranded corporate costs from the Pizza Hut exit linger, and tax rates drift up (Pillar Two, IRS posture). Leverage at ~3.5x limits flexibility.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the Taco Bell food-safety recall is live and its traffic recovery unproven, the IRS 2014 Tax Court case is a binary multi-billion exposure (only its expected value is in the bridge), and leverage is ~3.4x net debt/EBITDA. Base 50% because the post-divestiture portfolio is the higher-growth, higher-margin two brands with a long franchisor track record. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs both KFC international unit growth at the top of range and Taco Bell international to scale.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a pro forma ex-Pizza Hut base. YUM's value is its royalty stream; its negative book equity reflects returned capital, not impairment, so book-based models are not meaningful. Debt is deducted once, at the pro forma post-sale level; SBC (incl. withholding) is expensed with a flat share count. At ~27x pro forma unlevered owner FCF the market is pricing a high-quality franchisor at roughly the base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the value (cap-bound at 20x in base); a 1pp WACC change moves value by roughly 20%.
IRS 2014 reorganization claim (~$4.6bn incl. interest and penalties, ~$17/share) is carried at expected value only.
Pro forma ex-Pizza Hut base is estimated from segment disclosures (Pizza Hut TTM revenue/OP partly interpolated); stranded corporate costs post-sale could be larger than assumed.
Taco Bell US lettuce recall (July 2026) -- depth and duration of traffic loss not yet visible in reported numbers.
Geopolitical boycotts of Western brands in KFC's Middle East/SE Asia markets and FX on a ~90%-international KFC system.

sanity_check_review.fix_applied: None -- one fix pass considered and declined: the trip is a negative-book-equity artifact, not an overvaluation signal. Shareholders' equity has been negative since the 2016 leveraged recap/Yum China spin, so P/B is meaningless and 'more negative than the historical max' only says the deficit shrank (-7,107 vs -7,926 in FY2018) while the price rose. The multiples that mean something are inside their 10yr ranges: SBC-adjusted P/E 26.5x vs 27.6x average (20.3-41.3), EV/EBITDA 18.7x vs 20.3x average (12.6-27.9), P/S 4.8x vs 5.3x average. The two diagnosis candidates are also artifacts: the -1.3% 'through-cycle revenue CAGR' spans the 2016 Yum China spin-off and the 2016-18 refranchising that halved reported revenue (FY2015 13,105 incl. China -> FY2016 6,356), while post-2020 revenue CAGR is 7.8% and the 6.5% projected sits below it; and a WACC premium would charge risk twice on probability-weighted scenarios (owner-fcf.md section 8). Mid-cycle FCF is not applicable (franchisor royalties are not cyclical and FY0 is already normalized ex-Pizza Hut and ex-special items); the exit multiple already binds at the 20x cap in base and 15x in bear.
